planting.note: Divide or pot up offsets as new growth resumes in spring after the winter rest.

directions: Native to limestone cliffs and road cuts in the Mexican state of Oaxaca, this butterwort holds a flat rosette of broad, sticky pink-to-lavender leaves that trap gnats and small flies on their glistening mucilage. It is one of the two wild parents behind the popular hybrid 'Sethos', prized for passing on its strong pink leaf color and vigor. Large lavender to purple flowers with a pale throat rise on thin stalks well above the foliage in spring and summer. Grow it in a mineral-rich, peat-and-perlite mix kept evenly moist with rain or distilled water, in bright filtered light, and allow a cooler 2-to-3-month winter rest with reduced watering as it shrinks to a smaller, tighter succulent rosette.
